answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks using proof-of-location beaconing. Each agent authenticates by triangulating propagation delays against a sensor ridge, verifying its physical site whether near a city garden or a remote tundra. An attacker incurs unavoidable capital and hardware deployment costs for each distinct physical position faked. However, radio multipath distortion and atmospheric noise degrade timing precision, falsely rejecting legitimate co-located agents.
